header:
Date: 2027-03-09
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (Southport CTO), Priya Nair (Southport ML Lead), Samir Patel (Southport Platform)
Recording: cloud
Notes: discovery focused on model selection (open models), context length, multilingual and tool-calling/function-calling support, hosted vs dedicated vs private
summary: Southport AI is evaluating Redwood for LLM inference. Primary concerns: multi-language support, long context (32k+), tool-calling/function-calling for retrieval and code execution, and security (KMS, SOC2, VPC). They want benchmarks for a short list of open models and cost/latency comparisons across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private options. Next steps agreed: Redwood to run benchmarks and send pricing/security docs; customer to share prompts and infra constraints.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Security: KMS, SOC2, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, you here Evan, Priya, Samir?
[00:05] Evan: yeah thanks Maya, we appreciate it, big picture we're evaluating Redwood for inference, mainly open model support and options for private deployment
[00:12] Priya: hi, yes, main goals are low-latency for web chat, but also some long context batches for document understanding, plus multilingual. we have data in en, es, fr, pt, zh
[00:20] Maya: great, Diego and I will walk through model tradeoffs and hosting options, also want to capture your success criteria and constraints
[00:30] Diego: quick q, what's your expected p99 latency target for chat?
[00:35] Evan: around 200-300 ms for short-turn chat, for the long context tasks we can tolerate higher, maybe under 2s for 8k inputs, but for 32k context operations we expect more like 3-5s top
[00:50] Priya: also need deterministic behavior for retrieval-tool calls, function-calling must be reliable and not hallucinate endpoints
[00:58] Samir: infra wise we prefer VPC/private deployment eventually, but initially ok with hosted for quick start if data residency and KMS are fine
[01:07] Maya: noted. on models, customers often start with a smaller set — Llama 3 variants, Mistral mixes, and Mosaic/MosaicML weights — we can run benchmarks. open models tradeoff is typically latency/cost vs instruction-following quality
[01:20] Diego: I'll add that quantization and kernel choices change the economics; for example a quantized 8-bit Llama 3 70B can be significantly cheaper than a 70B fp16 on raw throughput, but may affect some instruction behaviors
[01:34] Evan: are you supporting 64k context? we have a project that may need 64k, maybe 128k later
[01:40] Diego: Redwood runtime supports long-context variants; hosted catalog currently includes models with up to 64k in production, and we have private deployments that can extend to 128k with careful kernel planning and memory configuration
[01:52] Priya: any differences in tool-calling across hosted vs private?
[01:56] Maya: same API surface, function-calling and tool endpoints behave the same; differences are around network egress, VPC routing for private, and integration with customer KMS — Private gives you full control over keys and networking
[02:10] Samir: okay, about KMS — we use AWS KMS and HSM for keys, need guaranteed separation of logs and encryption at rest, is that supported?
[02:18] Diego: yes, for Dedicated and Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; for Hosted we offer managed encryption and bring-your-own-key via supported KMS providers — we can provide SOC2 and audit artifacts for hosted as well
[02:32] Evan: cool, pricing — what's the delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
[02:36] Maya: Hosted is pay-as-you-go, good for evals and burst; Dedicated is reserved capacity, better for predictable throughput and lower unit costs once you hit commit levels. Private has a platform/license component and ops support cost. We'll send a detailed sheet
[02:49] Priya: do you have recommendations for multilingual tokenization? spm/byte-level? we've seen tokenization variance hurting cross-language latency and cost
[02:57] Diego: we typically recommend byte-level bpe or tokenizer matching the model; some models like Llama 3 are trained on specific tokenizers, Mistral tends to be more forgiving. We'll include tokenization impact in the benchmark report
[03:12] Evan: model list — which three would you recommend we benchmark?
[03:15] Maya: common combo: Llama 3 70B instruct, Mistral Mix (the 8x-style high-throughput variant), and Mosaic 65B quantized; we can swap in any other you prefer
[03:26] Priya: sounds good. also need to validate function-calling + retrieval chain: agent calls retrieval, retrieval returns docs, then tool-call to a code-exec sandbox — we want to see reliability and costs end-to-end
[03:40] Diego: we can run an agent-like pipeline in the benchmarks. note that caching (prefix and KV cache) dramatically reduces cost for repeated contexts; we'll surface that too
[03:51] Evan: what's Redwood's support for continuous batching and latency SLOs?
[03:55] Maya: runtime is designed for continuous batching; you can configure latency SLOs per route and have smart routing fallbacks to smaller models if SLOs are at risk
[04:08] Samir: for private deployment, what's networking topology — do we deploy inside our VPC, or an on-prem cluster?
[04:15] Diego: both. Private supports VPC mode (customer control plane + private nodes) and on-prem appliance for air-gapped environments. We'll need to map ports, egress rules, and KMS endpoints in the security deep-dive
[04:28] Priya: any known hallucination differences across models on tool-calling tasks? we've seen some models try to call wrong functions or invent parameters
[04:36] Diego: yes, some models are more prone; we use prompt engineering, function schemas, and a verification step in the agent to reduce hallucinations. We'll include reliability metrics in the tests (false function calls per 1000 interactions)
[04:52] Evan: great, can you also capture token costs for multilingual prompts, e.g., zh vs en? tokenization will change cost math
[04:59] Diego: yep, we'll run tokenization-aware cost estimates and show per-language tokenization overheads
[05:07] Maya: timeline — we'd like to demo benchmarks next week and then a security deep-dive the week after. is that workable?
[05:12] Priya: yes, that works for our schedule
[05:15] Evan: stakeholders — myself, Priya for ML, Samir for infra, and Legal might join the security deep-dive
[05:23] Maya: ok noted. any questions on rollout or can we talk about integration patterns?
[05:27] Samir: integration — do you have an SDK or do people use REST? we prefer an SDK with typed function-calls and retries built in
[05:33] Maya: we have REST + SDKs in the major languages. SDKs include helpers for streaming, function-calling wrappers, and retry policies. We'll send links to SDK docs
[05:44] Priya: about model pinning and rollouts — we need to be able to pin a model version per route for experiments
[05:50] Diego: supported. Redwood console supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. We'll show the console controls during the demo
[05:58] Evan: any red flags on inferencing for code generation? we run internal code-gen tasks and need reproducible outputs for CI checks
[06:05] Diego: for reproducibility we recommend deterministic sampling configs, pinned model versions, and recording random seeds if needed. Quantization can slightly change outputs; we'll document delta for each quant profile
[06:20] Maya: quick recap of agreed next steps: we'll run the benchmark (Llama3 70B, Mistral Mix, Mosaic 65B quant), send pricing and security docs, and schedule deep-dive
[06:30] Priya: and we'll send prompt sets + languages and confirm infra constraints
[06:34] Evan: thanks, this was helpful
[06:36] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and deliverables
[06:40] Samir: bye
[06:42] Recording end

Notes on transcript: automated captions occasionally put 'Redwood Dedicate' or 'Redwood privet' but context makes meanings clear; some model names transcribed as 'Mistral mix' vs 'Mistral MX' depending on audio.
